content: Lenacapavir increases the levels or effects of medroxyprogesterone by influencing hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 enzyme metabolism. Exercise caution and monitor closely. Lenacapavir may also increase the effects of CYP3A4 substrates initiated within nine months after the last subcutaneous dose, potentially raising the risk of adverse reactions. Levoketoconazole increases the levels or effects of medroxyprogesterone by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. Medroxyprogesterone reduces the effects of liraglutide through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Caution and monitoring are recommended. Additionally, medroxyprogesterone may impair glucose tolerance, reducing the hypoglycemic effects of antidiabetic medications. Glycemic control should be monitored in diabetic patients. Lopinavir increases the levels or effects of medroxyprogesterone by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are necessary. Lumacaftor/ivacaftor decreases the levels or effects of medroxyprogesterone by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Contraceptive failure is possible; alternative contraceptive methods should be considered if available. Medroxyprogesterone reduces the effects of metformin through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Caution and monitoring are advised. Mitotane decreases medroxyprogesterone levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Mitotane is a strong inducer of CYP3A4, and dosage adjustments may be required when co-administered with CYP3A4 substrates. Monitor closely. Nafcillin decreases the levels or effects of medroxyprogesterone by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Contraceptive failure is possible; alternative methods should be used if available. Nefazodone increases the levels or effects of medroxyprogesterone by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are recommended. Nemolizumab decreases medroxyprogesterone levels by increasing CYP enzyme activity through cytokine suppression. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. Dosage adjustments may be necessary for narrow therapeutic index CYP substrates. Nevirapine decreases the levels or effects of medroxyprogesterone by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. Contraceptive failure is possible. Rifapentine decreases the levels or effects of medroxyprogesterone by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are necessary. Contraceptive failure is possible. Rucaparib increases the levels or effects of medroxyprogesterone by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are advised. Dosage adjustments for CYP3A4 substrates may be required. Siponimod and medroxyprogesterone both increase immunosuppressive effects, raising the risk of infection. Caution and monitoring are recommended during and after therapy. Consider the half-life and mechanism of action of drugs with prolonged immune effects to avoid additive immunosuppressive effects. St. John’s Wort decreases the levels or effects of medroxyprogesterone by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. Contraceptive failure is possible. Stiripentol affects medroxyprogesterone levels by inhibiting and inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are necessary. Dosage adjustments for CYP3A4 substrates may be required. Tazemetostat decreases the levels or effects of medroxyprogesterone by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. Tecovirimat decreases the levels or effects of medroxyprogesterone by weakly inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitor sensitive CYP3A4 substrates for effectiveness if co-administered. Tesamorelin decreases the levels or effects of medroxyprogesterone by altering metabolism. Caution and monitoring are recommended. Alternative contraceptive methods should be used. Maitake mushroom increases the effects of medroxyprogesterone through pharmacodynamic synergy. The clinical significance is unknown. Maitake has demonstrated anti-tumor effects in animal and in vitro studies. Medroxyprogesterone decreases taurine levels through an unspecified mechanism. The clinical significance is unknown. Acitretin decreases the effects of medroxyprogesterone through an unknown mechanism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Contraceptive failure may occur. Apalutamide, a strong CYP3A4 inducer, can lower exposure to CYP3A4 substrates. Evaluate for therapeutic loss if co-administration is necessary. Alternative methods should be considered if available. Bosentan decreases the levels or effects of medroxyprogesterone by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Contraceptive failure is possible; alternative methods should be used if available. Brigatinib decreases the levels or effects of medroxyprogesterone by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Brigatinib can reduce hormonal contraceptive efficacy and may cause fetal harm. Women should use effective non-hormonal contraception during treatment and for at least four months after the last dose. Clobazam decreases the levels or effects of medroxyprogesterone by weakly inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Hormonal contraceptive efficacy may be reduced. Additional non-hormonal contraception is recommended. Crofeler increases medroxyprogesterone levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 in the gut. Systemic inhibition is unlikely due to minimal absorption. Caution and monitoring are advised. Dabrafenib decreases the levels or effects of medroxyprogesterone by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are necessary. Darunavir increases medroxyprogesterone levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug.
